race_context: The School Town of Highland is the public school district for the town of Highland in Lake County, with its administration center at 9145 Kennedy Ave. {hl_meetings}{hl_min_jul26}. This guide did not verify a current enrollment figure. In July 2026 the district reported a 98% graduation rate and a 97% IREAD passing rate {hl_smith}.

The board has five members, all elected at large: President Patrick Krull, Vice President Robert Kuva, Secretary Erica Smith-Gomez, Victor A. Garcia and Richard Alyea {hl_board}{hl_min_jan26}. In 2022 voters filled three at-large seats, electing Garcia (3,931 votes), Smith-Gomez (3,782) and Kuva (3,584) over Carol Parker (2,820) and Richard (Rick) E Volbrecht Jr (2,491) {lc_2022}. In 2024 they filled two seats, electing Krull (4,099) and Rick Alyea (3,687) over Allencia Ballard (3,645) and Volbrecht (3,442) {lc_2024}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: the Lake County sample ballot says 'Vote for not more than Three (3)' in the School Town of Highland at-large race. The state list shows 'vote for 1' {lc_sample_hl}{in_list}. The three seats are those won in 2022. All three incumbents, Garcia, Kuva and Smith-Gomez, are running again. The fourth candidate is Volbrecht, who ran unsuccessfully in 2022 and 2024 {lc_sample_hl}{lc_2022}{lc_2024}. Krull and Alyea are not on this ballot {lc_2024}. On the ballot, Garcia and Smith-Gomez are listed as Independent, Volbrecht as Republican, and Kuva with no party {lc_sample_hl}.

Superintendent turnover (2026): on July 2, 2026 the board accepted the resignation of Dr. Brian Smith, superintendent for 13 years, and named Assistant Superintendent Dr. Ryan Erdelac interim superintendent {hl_min_jul2}{hl_smith}. Erdelac resigned as assistant superintendent effective Aug. 20, 2026 {hl_min_aug18}. On Aug. 18, 2026 the board voted to appoint Dr. John Schwuchow, a former elementary school teacher who said he was glad to be returning to Highland, as interim superintendent retroactive to Aug. 11 {hl_min_aug18}. The board president said a new posting and a hearing were required before Schwuchow could be made permanent {hl_min_aug18}. A public notice set a Sept. 14, 2026 hearing on a proposed three-year superintendent contract running from Sept. 1, 2026 to June 30, 2029. It lists a $193,500 salary and $242,159.97 in total annual compensation and benefits {hl_supt_notice}. The district's staff directory now lists Schwuchow as superintendent {hl_staff}.

August 2026 storm: after a severe storm on Aug. 11, 2026, the administration center lost power and the board postponed an Aug. 17 special meeting on the superintendent contract {hl_postpone}. On Aug. 25 the board voted to keep paying eligible non-certified employees for their regular workdays from Aug. 11 to Aug. 21 {hl_min_aug25}. The first day of school was Aug. 25 {hl_firstday}{hl_min_aug18}.

Budget, property taxes and referendums: in May 2023 Highland voters rejected the district's operating referendum, 2,416 votes (52.25%) to 2,208 (47.75%) {lc_2023}. The district had said it was losing revenue to declining enrollment and changing demographics and had the lowest school tax rate in the area {hl_ref2023}. Members of the public raised a possible referendum at board meetings in January 2026 and raised the 2023 referendum's failure in August 2026 {hl_min_jan26}{hl_min_aug18}. In February 2026 Garcia reported meeting Highland's legislators about challenges the district expects from Senate Enrolled Act 1 {hl_min_feb26}. On April 21, 2026 the board hired Policy Analytics to study property tax impacts and revenue {hl_min_apr26}. On July 21, 2026 it approved transferring up to $528,581.51 from the Debt Service Fund to the Operations Fund in 2026 {hl_min_jul26}. There is no Highland school question on the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot {lc_sample_hl}.

Facilities and bonds: projects from the 2025 general obligation bond include high school and middle school gym bleachers and HVAC. In July 2026 the board hired The Skillman Corporation ($110,450) to manage that work and raised Schmidt Associates' architectural fee from $170,000 to $227,357 {hl_min_jul26}. In September 2026 the board held hearings on a new bond for facility, athletic, safety and security improvements and for buses, equipment and technology {hl_go_hearing}. Its notice of preliminary determination lists a maximum of $6,800,000 over five years and estimates no net increase in the debt service tax rate as existing debt matures {hl_pd_notice}.

Other 2025–2026 items: in July 2026 the board approved a high school handbook change putting in place the state's 'bell-to-bell' personal device ban (SEA 78) {hl_min_jul26}. It also approved a $109,348.64 agreement with the Town of Highland for a school resource officer {hl_min_jul26}. In February 2026 Smith-Gomez reported that state special education funding had been cut in every category for the year {hl_min_feb26}. Members of the public raised the enrollment of out-of-district students at meetings in August 2025 and January 2026 {hl_min_aug25b}{hl_min_jan26}.

Forums: this guide found no candidate forums, questionnaires or news coverage of the 2026 Highland race. Three of the four candidates are sitting board members whose motions and votes appear in the board minutes cited here.
